2c9d519db3:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>T</c>his the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph
Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness
Erst on this feast-day merited to enter
Into his glory.

<h>S</h>aintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,
Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.
While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,
Quickened his being.

<h>S</h>ick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,
Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,
Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,
At his petition.

<h>W</h>hence we in chorus gladly do him honour,
Chanting his praises with devout affection,
That in his merits we may have a portion,
Now and forever.

<h>H</h>is be the glory, power and salvation,
Who over all things reigneth in the highest,
Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,
Onely and Trinal.
Amen.

<c>I</c>ste Conféssor Dómini sacrátus,
Festa plebs cuius celébrat per orbem,
Hódie lætus méruit secréta
Scándere cæli.

<h>Q</h>ui pius, prudens, húmilis, pudícus,
Sóbrius, castus fuit et quiétus,
Vita dum præsens vegetávit eius
Córporis artus.

Membra languéntum modo sanitáti,
Quólibet morbo fúerint graváta,
Restituúntur.

Ipsius, hymnum canit hunc libénter:
Ut piis eius méritis iuvémur
Omne per ævum.

<h>S</h>it salus illi, decus atque virtus,
Qui supra cæli résidens cacúmen,
Tótius mundi máchinam gubérnat
Trinus et unus.
Amen.

thy bishops’ fadeless crown, draw near:

Today attained a glorious fame;
Whose yearly feast, in solemn state,
Thy faithful people celebrate.

<h>T</h>he world and all its boasted good,
As vain and passing, he eschewed;
And therefore with angelic bands,
In endless joy forever stands.

<h>G</h>rant then that we, most gracious God,
May follow in the steps he trod:
And, at his prayer, thy servants free
From stain of all iniquity.

All glory, praise, and thanks we bring:
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.

Quólibet morbo fúerint graváta,

Omne per ævum.

Trinus et unus.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>T</c>his the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph
Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness
Erst on this feast-day merited to enter
Into his glory.

<h>S</h>aintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,
Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.
While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,
Quickened his being.

<h>S</h>ick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,
Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,
Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,
At his petition.

<h>W</h>hence we in chorus gladly do him honour,
Chanting his praises with devout affection,
That in his merits we may have a portion,
Now and forever.

<h>H</h>is be the glory, power and salvation,
Who over all things reigneth in the highest,
Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,
Onely and Trinal.
Amen.

<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>I</c>ste Conféssor Dómini sacrátus,
Festa plebs cuius celébrat per orbem,
Hac die lætus méruit suprémos
Laudis honóres.

<h>Q</h>ui pius, prudens, húmilis, pudícus,
Sóbrius, castus fuit et quiétus,
Vita dum præsens vegetávit eius
Córporis artus.

<h>O</h>b sacrum cuius túmulum frequénter
Membra languéntum modo sanitáti,
Quólibet morbo fúerint graváta,
Restituúntur.

<h>U</h>nde nunc noster chorus in honórem
Ipsius, hymnum canit hunc libénter:
Ut piis eius méritis iuvémur
Omne per ævum.

<h>S</h>it salus illi, decus atque virtus,
Qui supra cæli résidens cacúmen,
Tótius mundi máchinam gubérnat
Trinus et unus.
Amen.

<c>V</c>ox clara ecce íntonat,

54be439041:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>C</c>elestial Word, to this our earth
Sent down from God's eternal clime,
To save mankind by mortal birth
Into a world of change and time;

<h>E</h>nlighten our hearts; vain hopes destroy;
And in thy love's consuming fire
Fill all the soul with heavenly joy,
And melt the dross of low desire.

<h>S</h>o when the Judge of quick and dead
Shall bid his awful summons come,
To whelm the guilty soul with dread,
And call the blessed to their home.

<h>S</h>aved from the whirling, black abyss,
Forevermore to us be given
To share the feast of saintly bliss,
And see the face of God in heaven.

<h>T</h>o God the Father and the Son
Our songs with one accord we raise;
And to the Holy Spirit, One
With them, be ever equal praise
Amen.

Their endless hope to Thee that bow;

How, taking form of humankind,
Born of a Virgin undefiled,

Through every year in long array,
That Thou, salvation’s source alone,
Proceedest from the Father’s throne.

And all that earth’s wide realms contain,
With joyous voice now loudly sing
The glory of their new-born King.

From sin redeemed, are marked for God,
On this the day that saw Thy birth,
Sing the new song of ransomed earth.

Eternal praise and glory be,
Whom with the Father we adore
And Holy Ghost forevermore.

<c>F</c>rom lands that see the sun arise
To earth's remotest boundaries,
The Virgin-born today we sing,

To take a servant's form He came,
That, liberating flesh by flesh,
Whom He had made might live afresh.

Celestial grace hath found its home;

The cradle did He not abhor;
By milk in infant portions fed,
Who gives e'en fowls their daily bread.

The Angels sang to God on high,
What time to shepherds, watching lone,
They made creation's Shepherd known.

All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.

<r>Heb 11:33</r>
<c>S</c>ancti per fidem vicérunt regna, operáti sunt justítiam, adépti sunt repromissiónes, in Christo Jesu Dómino nostro.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>S</c>ing, O sons of the Church sounding the martyrs' praise!
God's true soldiers applaud, who, in their weary days,
Won bright trophies of good, glad be the voice ye raise,
While these heroes of Christ ye sing!

<h>T</h>hey, while yet in the world were by the world abhorred;
Felt how fading the joys, fleeting the wealth it stored;
Spurned all pleasure for thee, and at thy call, O Lord,
Came forth strong in thy name, as King.

<h>L</h>ord, how bravely they bore fury and pain for thee!
Scourge, rod, sword, and the rack strongly endured; but free
Sang out, bold in thy love, longing on high to be;
Earth's might never their souls could bend.

<h>W</h>hile they, shedding their blood, victims for Jesus fell,
No sound out of their lips came of their throes to tell;
Bowed low, patient and meek, loving the Lord so well,
Turned they still to the Christ, their friend.

<h>W</h>hat joys, bright with the blood shed for thy love they share,
Those brave martyrs of thine crowned with thy laurels rare;
Man's tongue never can tell, never can half declare,
How pure now is their bliss above!

<h>Y</h>et we, Father on high, God of eternal might,
Lift weak voices in prayer asking for peace and light;
Cleanse thou out of our hearts every stain and blight,
So our songs may be songs of love.
Amen.

6d6abcf9e2:
<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>Q</c>uem terra, pontus, ǽthera
Colunt, adórant, prædicant,
Trinam regéntem máchinam,
Claustrum Maríæ báiulat.

<h>C</h>ui luna, sol, et ómnia
Desérviunt per témpora,
Perfúsa cæli grátia,
Gestant puéllæ víscera.

<h>B</h>eáta Mater múnere,
Cuius supérnus ártifex
Mundum pugíllo cóntinens,
Ventris sub arca clausus est.

<h>B</h>eáta cæli núntio,
Fœcúnda sancto Spíritu,
Desiderátus géntibus,
Cuius per alvum fusus est.

<h>I</h>esu, tibi sit glória,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.

<c>G</c>rant us, we beseech thee, O Almighty God, ever to think such things as be reasonable, and in every word and work of ours, to do always that is well pleasing in thy sight.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
5e2c70dabd:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>T</c>he God whom earth, and sea, and sky
Adore, and laud, and magnify,
Who o'er their threefold fabric reigns,
The Virgin's spotless womb contains.

<h>T</h>he God, whose will by moon and sun
And all things in due course is done,
Is borne upon a maiden's breast,
By fullest heavenly grace possest.

<h>H</h>ow blest that mother, in whose shrine
The great artificer divine,
Whose hand contains the earth and sky,
Vouchsafed, as in his ark, to lie.

<h>B</h>lest, in the message Gabriel brought;
Blest, by the work the Spirit wrought;
From whom the great desire of earth
Took human flesh and human birth.

<h>A</h>ll honour, laud, and glory be,
O Jesu, Virgin-born to thee;
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.

<c>t</c>o Matthew
<r>Matt 5:13-19</r>
<c>A</c>t that time Jesus said to His disciples: “You are the salt of the earth; but if the salt loses its strength, what shall it be salted with? It is no longer of any use but to be thrown out and trodden underfoot by men. You are the light of the world. A city set on a mountain cannot be hidden. Neither do men light a lamp and put it under the measure, but upon the lampstand, so as to give light to all in the house. Even so let your light shine before men, in order that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father in heaven. Do not think that I have come to destroy the Law or the Prophets. I have not come to destroy, but to fulfill. For amen I say to you, till heaven and earth pass away, not one jot or one tittle shall be lost from the Law till all things have been accomplished. Therefore whoever does away with one of these least commandments, and so teaches men, shall be called least in the kingdom of heaven; but whoever carries them out and teaches them, he shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<c>K</c>ýrie, eléison. Christe, eléison. Kýrie, eléison.
<n><k>Pater Noster</k> dicitur secreto usque ad <k>Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:</k></n>
<c>P</c>ater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:

<c>O</c>rémus.

<h>Q</h>ui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<c>I</c>n illo témpore: Venit Iesus in partes Cæsaréæ Philíppi, et interrogábat discípulos suos, dicens: Quem dicunt hómines esse Fílium hóminis? At illi dixérunt: Alii Ioánnem Baptístam, alii autem Elíam, álii vero Ieremíam, aut unum ex prophétis. Dicit illis Iesus: Vos autem quem me esse dícitis? Respóndens Simon Petrus, dixit: Tu es Christus, Fílius Dei vivi. Respóndens autem Iesus, dixit ei: Beátus es, Simon Bar Iona: quia caro et sanguis non revelávit tibi, sed Pater meus, qui in cœlis est. Et ego dico tibi, quia tu es Petrus, et super hanc petram ædificábo Ecclésiam meam, et portæ ínferi non prævalébunt advérsus eam. Et tibi dabo claves regni cœlórum. Et quodcúmque ligáveris super terram, erit ligátum et in cœlis: et quodcúmque sólveris super terram, erit solútum et in cœlis.

<r>Eph 2:19-20</r>
<c>N</c>ow therefore you are no more strangers and foreigners; but you are fellow citizens with the saints, and the domestics of God, built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<c>N</c>ow let the earth with joy resound,
And heaven the chant re-echo round;
Nor heaven nor earth too high can raise
The great Apostles' glorious praise.

<h>O</h> ye who, throned in glory dread,
Shall judge the living and the dead,
Lights of the world forevermore!
To you the suppliant prayer we pour.

<h>Y</h>e close the sacred gates on high;
At your command apart they fly:
Oh! loose for us the guilty chain
We strive to break, and strive in vain.

<h>S</h>ickness and health your voice obey;
At your command they go or stay:
From sin's disease our souls restore;
In good confirm us more and more.

<h>S</h>o when the world is at its end,
And Christ to judgement shall descend,
May we be called those joys to see
Prepared from all eternity.

<h>P</h>raise to the Father, with the Son,
And Holy Spirit, Three in One;
As ever was in ages past,
And so shall be while ages last.
Amen.

<c>V</c>eni, redémptor géntium,
Osténde partum Vírginis:
Mirétur omne sæculum:
Talis decet partus Deum.

<h>N</h>on ex viríli sémine,
Sed mýstico spirámine
Verbum Dei factum est caro
Fructúsque ventris flóruit.

<h>A</h>lvus tuméscit Vírginis,
Claustrum pudóris pérmanet,
Vexílla virtútum micant,
Versátur in templo Deus.

<h>P</h>rocédat e thálamo suo,
Pudóris aula régia,
Géminæ gigas substántiæ
Alácris ut currat viam.

<h>Æ</h>quális ætérno Patri,
Carnis tropæo cíngere,
Infírma nostri córporis
Virtúte firmans pérpeti.

<h>P</h>ræsépe iam fulget tuum
Luménque nox spirat novum,
Quod nulla nox intérpolet
Fidéque iugi lúceat.

<h>G</h>lória tibi, Dómine,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre, et Sancto Spíritu,

<c>G</c>od, who, at sundry times and in diverse manners, spoke in times past to the fathers by the prophets, last of all, in these days hath spoken to us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the world.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>V</c>eni, redémptor géntium,
Osténde partum Vírginis:
Mirétur omne sæculum:
Talis decet partus Deum.

<h>N</h>on ex viríli sémine,
Sed mýstico spirámine
Verbum Dei factum est caro
Fructúsque ventris flóruit.

<h>A</h>lvus tuméscit Vírginis,
Claustrum pudóris pérmanet,
Vexílla virtútum micant,
Versátur in templo Deus.

<h>P</h>rocédat e thálamo suo,
Pudóris aula régia,
Géminæ gigas substántiæ
Alácris ut currat viam.

<h>Æ</h>quális ætérno Patri,
Carnis tropæo cíngere,
Infírma nostri córporis
Virtúte firmans pérpeti.

<h>P</h>ræsépe jam fulget tuum
Luménque nox spirat novum,
Quod nulla nox intérpolet
Fidéque jugi lúceat.

<h>A</h>ll honour, praise and glory be,
O Jesu, Virgin-Born, to thee;
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father, and to Paraclete.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> The Lord is as a bridegroom.
<r>℟.</r> Coming out of his chamber.

c2e5da3161:
<h>Oratio</h>
<c>K</c>ýrie, eléison. Christe, eléison. Kýrie, eléison.
<n><k>Pater Noster</k> dicitur secreto usque ad <k>Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:</k></n>
<c>P</c>ater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
<r>℣.</r> Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
<r>℟.</r> Sed líbera nos a malo.

<r>℣.</r> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>eus, qui salútis ætérnæ, beátæ Maríæ virginitáte fecúnda, humáno géneri prǽmia præstitísti: tríbue, quǽsumus; ut ipsam pro nobis intercédere sentiámus, per quam merúimus auctórem vitæ suscípere, Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum Fílium tuum:
<h>Q</h>ui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
bf9086fcec:
<h>Prayer</h>
<c>L</c>ord have mercy upon us, Christ have mercy upon us, Lord have mercy upon us.
<n><k>Our Father</k> is said silently until <k>And lead us not into temptation:</k>.</n>
<c>O</c>ur Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.
<r>℣.</r> And lead us not into temptation:
<r>℟.</r> But deliver us from evil.

<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> God, Who, by the fruitful virginity of the Blessed Mary, hast given unto mankind the rewards of everlasting life; grant, we beseech thee, that we may continually feel the might of her intercession, through whom we have worthily received the Author of our life, our Lord Jesus Christ, thy Son:
<h>W</h>ho with thee liveth and reigneth, in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Hymn</h>
<c>T</c>he fast, as taught by holy lore,
We keep in solemn course once more:
The fast to all men known, and bound
In forty days of yearly round.

<h>T</h>he law and seers that were of old
In diverse ways this Lent foretold,
Which Christ, all seasons’ King and Guide,
In after ages sanctified.

<h>M</h>ore sparing therefore let us make
The words we speak, the food we take,
Our sleep and mirth, —and closer barred
Be every sense in holy guard.

<h>A</h>void the evil thoughts that roll
Like waters o’er the heedless soul;
Nor let the foe occasion find
Our souls in slavery to bind.

<h>I</h>n prayer together let us fall,
And cry for mercy, one and all,
And weep before the Judge’s feet,
And his avenging wrath entreat.

<h>T</h>hy grace have we offended sore,
By sins, O God, which we deplore;
But pour upon us from on high,
O pardoning One, thy clemency.

<h>R</h>emember thou, though frail we be,
That yet thine handiwork are we;
Nor let the honour of thy name
Be by another put to shame.

<h>F</h>orgive the sin that we have wrought;
Increase the good that we have sought:
That we at length, our wanderings o'er,
May please thee here and evermore.

<h>G</h>rant O thou Blessed Trinity,
Grant, O Essential Unity,
That this our fast of forty days
May work our profit and thy praise.
Amen.

Quo démptio fit críminum.

<h>D</h>ies venit, dies tua,
In qua reflórent ómnia:
Lætémur in hac ad tuam
Per hanc redúcti grátiam.

<h>T</h>e rerum univérsitas,
Clemens, adóret, Trínitas,
Et nos novi per véniam,
Novum canámus cánticum.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Scuto circúmdabit te véritas eius.
<r>℟.</r> Non timébis a timóre noctúrno.
36ea047503:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>Joel 2:12-13</r>
<c>B</c>e converted to me with all your heart, in fasting, and in weeping, and in mourning. And rend your hearts, and not your garments, said the almighty Lord.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>O</c> kind Creator, bow thine ear
To mark the cry, to know the tear
Before thy throne of mercy spent
In this thy holy fast of Lent.

<h>O</h>ur hearts are open, Lord, to thee:
Thou knowest our infirmity;
Pour out on all who seek thy face
Abundance of thy pardoning grace.

<h>O</h>ur sins are many, this we know;
Spare us, good Lord, thy mercy show;
And for the honour of thy name
Our fainting souls to life reclaim.

<h>G</h>ive us the self-control that springs
From discipline of outward things,
That fasting inward secretly
The soul may purely dwell with thee.

<h>W</h>e pray thee, Holy Trinity,
One God, unchanging Unity,
That we from this our abstinence
May reap the fruits of penitence.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> God hath given His Angels charge over thee.
<r>℟.</r> To keep thee in all thy ways.

a8f191c38e:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>S</c>ing, my tongue, the glorious battle
Sing the last, the dread affray;
O'er the cross, the victor's trophy,
Sound the high triumphal lay:
Tell how Christ, the world's Redeemer,
As a victim won the day.

<h>G</h>od, his Maker, sorely grieving
That the first-made Adam fell,
When he ate the fruit of sorrow,
Whose reward was death and hell,
Noted then this wood, the ruin
Of the ancient wood to quell.

<h>F</h>or the work of our salvation
Needs would have his order so,
And the multiform deceiver's
Art by art would overthrow,
And from thence would bring the med'cine
Whence the insult of the foe.

<h>W</h>herefore, when the sacred fullness
Of the appointed time was come,
This world's Maker left his Father,
Sent the heav'nly mansion from,
And proceeded, God Incarnate,
Of the Virgin's holy womb.

<h>W</h>eeps the infant in the manger
That in Bethlehem's stable stands;
And his limbs the Virgin Mother
Doth compose in swaddling bands,
Meetly thus in linen folding
Of her God the feet and hands.

<h>T</h>o the Trinity be glory
Everlasting, as is meet;
Equal to the Father, equal
To the Son, and Paraclete:
Trinal Unity, whose praises
All created things repeat.
Amen.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>L</c>ustris sex qui iam peráctis,
Tempus implens córporis,
Se volénte natus ad hoc,
Passióni déditus,
Agnus in Crucis levátur
Immolándus stípite.

<h>H</h>ic acétum, fel, arúndo,
Sputa, clavi, láncea:
Mite corpus perforátur,
Sanguis, unda prófluit:
Terra, pontus, astra, mundus,
Quo lavántur flúmine!

<h>C</h>rux fidélis, inter omnes
Arbor una nóbilis:
Nulla silva talem profert
Fronde, flore, gérmine:
Dulce lignum, dulces clavos,
Dulce pondus sústinet.

<h>F</h>lecte ramos, arbor alta,
Tensa laxa víscera,
Et rigor lentéscat ille,
Quem dedit natívitas:
Ut supérni membra Regis
Miti tendas stípite.

<h>S</h>ola digna tu fuísti
Ferre sæcli prétium,
Atque portum præparáre
Nauta mundo náufrago,
Quem sacer cruor perúnxit,
Fusus Agni córpore.

<h>G</h>lória et honor Deo
Usquequáque altíssimo:
Una Patri, Filióque,
Inclyto Paráclito:
Cui laus est et potéstas
Per ætérna sǽcula.

<r>Jer 11:20</r>
<c>B</c>ut thou, O Lord of Sabaoth, who judgest justly, and triest the reins and hearts, let me see thy revenge on them: for to thee I have revealed my cause, O Lord my God.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>A</c>broad the regal banners fly,
Now shines the cross’s mystery;
Upon it Life did death endure,
And yet by death did life procure.

<h>W</h>ho, wounded with a direful spear,
Did, purposely to wash us clear
From stain of sin, pour out a flood
Of precious water mixed with blood.

<h>T</h>hat which the prophet-king of old
Hath in mysterious verse foretold,
Is now accomplished, whilst we see
God ruling nations from a tree.

<h>O</h> lovely and refulgent tree,
Adorned with purpled majesty;
Culled from a worthy stock, to bear
Those limbs which sanctifièd were.

<h>B</h>lest tree, whose happy branches bore
The wealth that did the world restore;
The beam that did that body weigh
Which raised up hell’s expected prey.

<r>The following verse is said on bended knee.</r>

<h>O</h> Cross, our one reliance, hail!
This holy Passiontide avail
To give fresh merit to the saint,
And pardon to the penitent.

<h>B</h>lest Trinity, salvation’s spring,
May every soul thy praises sing;
To those thou grantest conquest by
The holy cross, rewards apply.
Amen.

<r>℟.</r> Rescue me from the unjust man.

<c>T</c>u autem, Dómine Sábaoth, qui iúdicas iuste, et probas renes et corda, vídeam ultiónem tuam ex eis: tibi enim revelávi causam meam, Dómine, Deus meus.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>V</c>exílla Regis pródeunt:
Fulget Crucis mystérium,
Quo carne carnis Cónditor
Suspénsus est patíbulo.

<h>Q</h>uo vulnerátus ínsuper
Mucróne diro lánceæ,
Ut nos laváret crímine,
Manávit unda et sánguine.

<h>I</h>mpléta sunt quæ cóncinit
David fidéli cármine,
Dicens: In natiónibus
Regnávit a ligno Deus.

<h>A</h>rbor decóra et fúlgida,
Ornáta Regis púrpura,
Elécta digno stípite
Tam sancta membra tángere.

<h>B</h>eáta, cuius bráchiis
Sæcli pepéndit prétium,
Statéra facta córporis,
Prædámque tulit tártari.

<r>Sequens stropha dicitur flexis genibus.</r>

<h>O</h> Crux, ave, spes única,
Hoc Passiónis témpore
Auge piis iustítiam,
Reísque dona véniam.

<h>T</h>e summa, Deus, Trínitas,
Colláudet omnis spíritus:
Quos per Crucis mystérium
Salvas, rege per sǽcula.
Amen.

aa1a71587c:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>Jer 11:20</r>
<c>B</c>ut thou, O Lord of Sabaoth, who judgest justly, and triest the reins and hearts, let me see thy revenge on them: for to thee I have revealed my cause, O Lord my God.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>T</c>hirty years among us dwelling,
His appointed time fulfilled,
Born for this, he meets his passion,
For that this he freely willed:
On the cross the Lamb is lifted,
Where his life-blood shall be spilled.

<h>H</h>e endured the nails, the spitting,
Vinegar, and spear, and reed;
From that holy body broken
Blood and water forth proceed:
Earth, and stars, and sky, and ocean,
By that flood from stain are free.

<h>F</h>aithful cross! above all other,
One and only noble tree!
None in foliage, none in blossom,
None in fruit thy peers may be;
Sweetest wood and sweetest iron!
Sweetest weight is hung on thee.

<h>B</h>end thy boughs, O tree of glory!
Thy relaxing sinews bend;
For awhile the ancient rigour,
That thy birth bestowed, suspend;
And the King of heavenly beauty
On thy bosom gently tend!

<h>T</h>hou alone wast counted worthy
This world's ransom to uphold;
For a shipwrecked race preparing
Harbour, like the ark of old;
With the sacred blood anointed
From the smitten Lamb that rolled.

<h>T</h>o the Trinity be glory
Everlasting, as is meet;
Equal to the Father, equal
To the Son, and Paraclete:
Trinal Unity, whose praises
All created things repeat.
Amen.

<r>℟.</r> And defend me from them that rise up against me.

<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>P</c>ange, lingua, gloriósi
Prœlium certáminis,
Et super Crucis trophǽo
Dic triúmphum nóbilem,
Quáliter Redémptor orbis
Immolátus vícerit.

<h>D</h>e paréntis protoplásti
Fraude Factor cóndolens,
Quando pomi noxiális
Morsu in mortem córruit,
Ipse lignum tunc notávit,
Damna ligni ut sólveret.

<h>H</h>oc opus nostræ salútis
Ordo depopóscerat,
Multifórmis proditóris
Ars ut artem fálleret,
Et medélam ferret inde,
Hostis unde lǽserat.

<h>Q</h>uando venit ergo sacri
Plenitúdo témporis,
Missus est ab arce Patris
Natus, orbis Cónditor,
Atque ventre virgináli
Carne amíctus pródiit.

<h>V</h>agit infans inter arcta
Cónditus præsépia:
Membra pannis involúta
Virgo Mater álligat:
Et manus, pedésque, et crura
Stricta cingit fáscia.

<h>G</h>lória, et honor Deo
Usqueqáque Altíssimo,
Una Patri, Filióque;
Inclyto Paráclito:
Cui laus est et potéstas,
Per ætérna sǽcula.
Amen.

<r>Ant.</r> Hail holy Queen, Mother of Mercy, our life, our sweetness, and our hope. To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve. <r>℟.</r> That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ. Alleluia.

<c>A</c>t the Lamb’s high feast we sing
Praise to our victorious King,

<h>Hymn</h>
<c>O</c> thou, the heavens' eternal King,
Creator, unto thee we sing,
With God the Father ever One,
Co-equal, co-eternal Son.

<h>T</h>hy hand, when first the world began,
Made in thine own pure image man,
And linked to Adam, sprung from earth,
A living soul of heavenly birth.

<h>A</h>nd when by craft the envious foe
Had marred thy noblest work below,
Clothed in our flesh, thou didst restore
The image thou hadst made before.

<h>S</h>o that thou might redeem man
Whom thou hadst made
And us to God might thou wouldst unite
Through thy union with the flesh.

<h>O</h>nce wast thou born of Mary's womb;
And now, new-born from out the tomb,
O Christ, thou bidd'st us rise with thee
From death to immortality.

<h>E</h>ternal Shepherd, thou dost lave
Thy flock in pure baptismal wave,
That mystic bath, that grave of sin,
Where ransomed souls new life begin.

<h>R</h>edeemer, thou for us didst deign
To hang upon the Cross of pain,
And give for us the lavish price
Of thine own blood in sacrifice.

<h>G</h>rant, Lord, in thee each faithful mind
Unceasing paschal joy may find;
And from the death of sin set free
Souls newly born to life by thee.

<h>T</h>o Thee Who, dead, again dost live,
All glory, Lord, Thy people give;
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.

<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> God, Whose Son hath humbled Himself, and Who hast through Him raised up the whole world, grant to thy faithful people everlasting joy; and as Thou hast delivered them from the bitter pains of eternal death, make them to be glad for ever in thy presence.

<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>Act. 1:1-2</r>
<c>T</c>he former treatise I made, O Theophilus, of all things which Jesus began to do and to teach, Until the day on which, giving commandments by the Holy Ghost to the apostles whom he had chosen, he was taken up.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>E</c>ternal Monarch, King most high,
Whose blood hath brought redemption nigh,
By whom the death of death was wrought,
And conquering grace's battle fought:

<h>A</h>scending by the starry road,
This day thou wentest home to God,
By heaven to power unending called,
And by no human hand installed.

<h>T</h>hat so, in nature's triple frame,
Each heavenly and each earthly name,
And things in hell's abyss abhorred,
May bend the knee and own him Lord.

<h>Y</h>ea, angels tremble when they see
How changed is our humanity;
That flesh hath purged what flesh had stained,
And God, the flesh of God, hath reigned.

<h>B</h>e thou our joy, O mighty Lord,
As thou wilt be our great reward;
Earth's joys to thee are nothing worth,
Thou joy and crown of heaven and earth.

<h>A</h>ll glory, Lord, to thee we pay,
Ascending o'er the stars today;
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Eleváta est, magnificéntia tua, allelúja.
<r>℟.</r> Super cælos, Deus, allelúja.

<h>Hymn</h>
<c>H</c>ail, thou who man's Redeemer art,
Jesu, the joy of every heart;
Great Maker of the world's wide frame,
And purest love's delight and flame:

<h>W</h>hat nameless mercy thee o'ercame,
To bear our load of sin and shame?
For guiltless, thou thy life didst give,
That sinful erring man might live.

<h>T</h>he realms of woe are forced by thee,
Its captives from their chains set free;
And thou, amid thy ransomed train,
At God's right hand dost victor reign.

<h>L</h>et mercy sweet with thee prevail,
To cure the wounds we now bewail;
Oh, bless us with thy holy sight,
And fill us with eternal light.

<h>O</h>ur guide, our way to heavenly rest,
Be thou the aim of every breast;
Be thou the soother of our tears,
Our sweet reward above the spheres.

<h>A</h>ll glory, Lord, to Thee we pay,
Ascending o'er the stars to-day;
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.

<r>℟.</r> Protect us under the shadow of thy wings, alleluia.

<h>A</h>scending by the starry road,
This day thou wentest home to God,
By heaven to power unending called,
And by no human hand installed.

<h>T</h>hat so, in nature's triple frame,
Each heavenly and each earthly name,
And things in hell's abyss abhorred,
May bend the knee and own him Lord.

<h>Y</h>ea, angels tremble when they see
How changed is our humanity;
That flesh hath purged what flesh had stained,
And God, the flesh of God, hath reigned.

<h>B</h>e thou our joy, O mighty Lord,
As thou wilt be our great reward;
Earth's joys to thee are nothing worth,
Thou joy and crown of heaven and earth.

<h>A</h>ll glory, Lord, to thee we pay,
Ascending o'er the stars today;
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.

Jesu, the joy of every heart;
Great Maker of the world's wide frame,
And purest love's delight and flame:

To bear our load of sin and shame?
For guiltless, thou thy life didst give,
That sinful erring man might live.

Its captives from their chains set free;

At God's right hand dost victor reign.

To cure the wounds we now bewail;

And fill us with eternal light.

Within our breasts once sanctified,

Henceforth calm seasons sending.

<h>Hymn</h>
<c>N</c>ow Christ, ascending whence he came,
Had mounted o'er the starry frame,
The Holy Ghost on man below,
The Father's promise, to bestow.

<h>T</h>he solemn time was drawing nigh,
Replete with heav'nly mystery,
On seven days' sevenfold circles borne,
That first and blessèd Whitsun-morn.

<h>W</h>hen the third hour shone all around,
There came a rushing mighty sound,
And told the Apostles, while in prayer,
That, as was promised, God was there.

<h>F</h>orth from the Father's light it came,
That beautiful and kindly flame:
To fill with fervour of his word
The spirits faithful to their Lord.

Within our breasts once sanctified,
Deign, Lord, to cast our sins aside,
Henceforth calm seasons sending.

From death to endless life restored;
Whom with the Father we adore,
And Holy Ghost, for evermore.
Amen.

<c>R</c>ound roll the weeks our hearts to greet,
With blissful joy returning;

In fashion like a tongue, to teach
That eloquent they are of speech,
Their hearts with true love yearning.

The gifts from heaven descending;

Deign, Lord, to cast our sins aside,
Henceforth calm seasons sending.

From death to endless life restored;
Whom with the Father we adore,
And Holy Ghost, for evermore.

<h>Hymn</h>
<n>The first verse of the following hymn is said genuflecting.</n>
<c>C</c>reator Spirit, all Divine,
Come, visit every soul of Thine,
And fill with Thy celestial flame
The hearts which Thou Thyself didst frame.

<h>O</h> gift of God, Thine is the sweet
Consoling name of Paraclete
And spring of life and fire and love
And unction flowing from above.

<h>T</h>he mystic sevenfold gifts are Thine,
Finger of God's right hand divine;
The Father's promise sent to teach
The tongue a rich and heavenly speech.

<h>K</h>indle with fire brought from above
Each sense, and fill our hearts with love;
And grant our flesh, so weak and frail,
The strength of Thine which cannot fail.

<h>D</h>rive far away our deadly foe,
And grant us Thy true peace to know;
So we, led by Thy guidance still,
May safely pass through every ill.

<h>T</h>o us, through Thee, the grace be shown
To know the Father and the Son;
And Spirit of Them both, may we
Forever rest our faith in Thee.

<h>T</h>o Sire and Son be praises meet,
And to the Holy Paraclete;
And may Christ send us from above
That Holy Spirit's gift of love.
Amen

<h>Prayer</h>
<c>L</c>ord have mercy upon us, Christ have mercy upon us, Lord have mercy upon us.
<n><k>Our Father</k> is said silently until <k>And lead us not into temptation:</k>.</n>
<c>O</c>ur Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.
<r>℣.</r> And lead us not into temptation:
<r>℟.</r> But deliver us from evil.

<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> God, the protector of all them that trust in thee, without whom nothing is strong, nothing is holy; increase and multiply upon us thy mercy, that thou being our ruler and guide, we may so pass through things temporal, that we finally lose not the things eternal.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<c>K</c>ýrie, eléison. Christe, eléison. Kýrie, eléison.
<n><k>Pater Noster</k> dicitur secreto usque ad <k>Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:</k></n>
<c>P</c>ater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
<r>℣.</r> Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
<r>℟.</r> Sed líbera nos a malo.

<r>℣.</r> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>P</c>rotéctor in te sperántium, Deus, sine quo nihil est válidum, nihil sanctum; multíplica super nos misericórdiam tuam; ut, te rectóre, te duce, sic transeámus per bona temporália, ut non amittámus ætérna.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
